Great foundation in Early Access to begin with. Highly recommended.

This game is probably my favorite game of all time. And it’s not even finished yet. The combat is visceral and challenging. You aren’t nuking mobs of enemies, spamming the same skill hoping for a slightly better version of the same gear you already have to drop from one of the copy and pasted enemies like in Diablo.   In fact, besides the camera angle, it’s nothing like Diablo. Not sure why ppl try to make that comparison. 

This game is completely unique. There is no other game out there that will scratch this itch. No it’s not like V Rising. No it’s not like Seven. 

The combat is tight.  Every encounter is a legitimate threat. The bosses are even more challenging. But surviving an encounter, or finally taking down that boss give you that same dopamine hit you feel when you beat some boss in Dark Souls or Bloodborne. 

The level design and exploration are second to none. Not a bunch of goofy puzzles (at least not yet). Just genuine exploration, discovering vital shortcuts and save points. The verticality of the level design is second to none. But it isn’t forced like assassins creed or Mario. It all feels so fluid and natural. 

There’s a light resource farming/base crafting aspect to the game as well. Which is something that immediately turns me off to games (again, why I say V Rising is nothing like this masterpiece). The farming for minerals or lumber, or foraging for food again feel completely natural. Every now and then you’ll want to craft some specific thing or weapon upgrade and realize “oh I need to go farm some X”. But in my experience, that’s super rare. I don’t chop down every tree or mine every node, and I always seem to have what I need. Whereas other games attempts at resource farming/survival elements break immersion (despite intending to make the game more realistic) No Rest For the Wicked has found away to adopt this system seamlessly. It doesn’t break the immersion, but rather immerses me even more into the world. 

Then there’s the world itself. The art style is so unique. The gothic environments of the city/villages, the caves, the forests, the beaches, and all the other environs found in the game feel like painting/comicbook came to life. Moonstudios has crafted a beautiful world in No Rest For the Wicked, without compromising on atmosphere. You can be fighting for your life in the moonlit woods, or strolling through golden fields of sunflowers.  Again, a completely immersive experience.  

In short, there has never been a game like No Rest For the Wicked. There’s a lot of cynical critics on here that played the Early Access when it first launched and wrote the game off completely. But mark my words, this will be GOTY when it drops.

Absolutely fantastic art, voice acting and level design with solid on paper game mechanics that can be extremely frustrating to play largely due to certain game design issues that feel unpolished and lacking. This game has a lot going for it, but currently has foundational issues that constantly irritate me and take the fun out of the play experience. I'm just going to list the negatives in hopes that the devs might consider some changes.  Almost all my grievances are combat, movement or camera related. 

1) Constantly feel the need to rotate my camera angle but unable to.  Going "South" or towards bottom screen corners usually results in getting shot or attacked from off-screen by enemies unseen or accidentally dropping off a cliff.
2) Character and stamina/focus meter becomes obscured behind walls and objects leading to loss of control especially in combat.
3) Deeply wish I could zoom out more but this is mostly due to not being able to rotate the camera to see what is in front of me.
4) Auto-jump constantly kills me. Trying to climb down a ladder or mount a ledge the character often leaps off a cliff without my authorization. Sometimes the auto-jump fails to jump entirely when jumping is necessary  to clear a gap.
5) Movement over terrain is inconsistent. Sometimes I can climb up a rock or wall or similar object instantly and with ease, and sometimes I'm bumping up against the same object 50 times trying to redo what I've previously done, just trying to get on top.
6) Constantly feel the need to strafe or side-step, but no ability to do so. Would be useful both in combat and out, such as trying to get the character into the exact spot to open a chest or Press E to talk to someone.
7) Too small a box for engaging chests and people for interaction. I'm constantly bumping into chests, winding around them and walking over them trying to get the E to open to work; same goes for interacting with npcs. 
8) Enemy attacks track player unrealistically, breaking immersion and suspension of disbelief.  Arrows and bombs will curve as if heat-seeking in on the player and sometimes enemies jumping thru the air will rotate their attack midair and curve their jump to land where the player dodged to. 
9) Targeting system is terrible. Sometimes locks on, sometimes lock turns off, sometimes I can't turn off the lock and can't change targets. Rune attacks miss even when target is 1 meter away targeted and cursor is hovering over target. Sometimes Rune attacks shoot off to the side of the target. No consistency means loss of agency. I have no idea why my character is attacking in the opposite direction of my target and no my cursor is not directing the attack there.
10) Back-stab mechanic included but useless sneaking or crouching mechanic. I was hoping to play as a roguish character sneaking and backstabbing but there is no grass to hide in, no shadows, etc, and crouch-sneaking in the open obviously does nothing. Very, very circumstantial skill, especially considering some enemies are immune to back-stab.  Gave up on that build immediately. 
11) A lot of Parry windows feel way too late. For example, with spear and lance wielding types sometimes the lance model will penetrate thru me and then my parry takes effect after. But if I try and parry before the lance hits me I'm too early. Immersion broken. 
12)  Climbing vines movement is terrible. Doesn't move as directed, stutters, sometimes just falls off even though stamina is available.
13) Ridiculous weights for items. Revise all the weights. 10lb cloth gloves? 20lb jute leggings? 20lb leather cap? o_0
14) Esoteric damage vs armor system. I don't know how it works, but I know how it feels, and it doesn't feel like more armor actually mitigates damage.  
15) Lack of Difficulty scale. Sometimes I come home after work and I want to relax and enjoy the game, but instead it just stresses me out. I like a challenge too sometimes, but I would enjoy playing this on Normal or Easy Difficulty and not just Hard. In my experience, the grunts are often harder than the bosses. XD
16)  I'm not keen on the animations, but I supposed they match the game style.  
17) Running high end AMD hardware and the game often stutters, especially the cursor or mouse leading to sudden death. Game crashes frequently when using whispers to fast travel. 

To finish off, I'll restate some pros. Fantastic level design! Incredible portraits, 2D art and texture painting. Excellent voice acting and story telling. Great world building. It's a great start and still feels Early Access. Hoping they'll really polish this off and not just take their money and leave it as is. Thumbs up? Initially I thought yes. But I can't recommend the game in its early access state with the above issues.

After 900+ hours, I can confidently say No Rest for the Wicked is one of the most unique action RPGs I’ve played in years, and it’s absolutely a masterpiece in the making. It’s basically a Souls-like at heart, but with an isometric camera and a world that rewards exploration the way modern games rarely do. It doesn’t hold your hand, it doesn’t feel like a checklist, it feels like an actual adventure where you get stronger because you learned the game and because you went out of your way to discover things, not because the UI told you to.

The combat is the main reason I kept coming back. Every weapon has weight and rhythm, and even similar weapon types can feel different because of their movesets and animations. Learning enemy patterns, timing parries, managing stamina, and choosing when to spend Focus on rune attacks makes every fight feel deliberate. Build variety is also insane, you can go heavy claymore, fast dual daggers, tanky elemental setups, faith builds, battle-mage wand playstyles, and more, and each one genuinely changes how the game feels. I’ve replayed the whole thing multiple times on different realms, and it stayed fresh because the systems are deep enough to support it.

The world and level design are also a huge highlight. Isola Sacra is dense, vertical, and full of shortcuts and hidden paths, and the art style is honestly one of the best I’ve seen in an RPG. Sacrament is more than a menu hub, rebuilding the town, upgrading vendors, and even housing makes the game feel lived-in and personal. The gathering and crafting loop is also tied directly to survival, food is your healing, so preparing for a run actually matters. That said, this is also where some frustration shows up, inventory and storage can be annoying, and the grind can sometimes feel like a second job if you’re trying to min-max gear.

Co-op is optional, but it’s genuinely fun. Progression feels shared, combat becomes more tactical with different roles, and it adds a nice sense of companionship without ruining the atmosphere.

Now the early access part. This game has the bones of something legendary, but it still needs more meaningful side content. NPCs and the world have the vibe of deeper stories, but outside the main arc it can feel too quiet, with limited side quests and some repetitive bounty-style content. Also, difficulty settings don’t always feel like they change the experience in a meaningful way, once you learn the mechanics and upgrade your gear, the challenge drops off no matter what mode you pick, so I’d love to see a more cohesive long-term difficulty curve.

Even with those issues, I still fully recommend it if you like Souls-likes, action RPGs, and exploration-heavy games. If you can handle early access rough edges and you want to be part of a game that’s clearly building toward something bigger, this is absolutely worth it.

The creators of Ori have once again delivered a beautiful and engaging game — one that's worth buying even in early access, if only to help the developers stay independent and afloat. No Rest for the Wicked is an excellent ARPG with a dash of Dark Souls-style combat, where each encounter isn’t about wiping out everything in sight but rather focused duels involving dodges, well-timed skills, and counterattacks. But don’t be scared off by the difficulty — the game is still quite approachable, and any enemy can be defeated without needing a hundred tries.

The game also boasts a stunning visual style — it looks like a living watercolor painting. It’s especially impressive in HDR. Plus, it features a solid physics system, which is a rare treat in modern games.

All in all, support the developers. This is a truly unique and well-crafted game that deserves to make it to full release.

Absolutely brilliant. Stunning. One of the best games I’ve played in years, across all platforms.

Gorgeous visuals, infinite artistic cleverness in the tiniest details of the game world. A perfect flow between exploration, story, and satisfying battles. A fantasy world in a nutshell that respects the player — not too easy, not too hard, no Souls-like pain, just the right level of challenge without frustration.

And those locations… I genuinely don’t understand how such complex spaces were designed — so many layers of traversal, new discoveries at every step, shortcuts revealed at the perfect moments, pure admiration for the creativity.

It’s an absolutely perfect example of how modern games should look and feel. How narrative should flow. Just a small example: when you arrive at a quest marker, you don’t see a static NPC waiting with an icon above their head. The NPCs are alive within the game’s narrative — they don’t wait for you to click on them. You step into the middle of an ongoing conversation. The characters aren’t just tools for gameplay actions; they truly feel like part of a living world. And that level of attention to detail exists in every aspect. The way fallen leaves and stones react to the player and world events. The way your character moves and sounds in different equipment. The way friendly fire affects enemies. The way enemies make mistakes. Such talent...

The game needs polishing, especially in player landing animations and in the in-game FAQ/codex — there needs to be more clarity around how certain mechanics work, particularly equipment crafting. But I’m sure all the occasional imperfections of early access will evolve into the best possible solutions by release (hopefully with protective locks on important items=).

And at first sight, you might think there are too many systems, too many things to do, too much to craft and build, too many places to go. But very soon, you want to do everything. And suddenly you find yourself playing at five in the morning, not wanting to stop. Even the current version of the endgame is interesting and challenging. It pushes you to create a perfect build — and then to experiment with many different builds. And they’re all so cool, so distinct in how they feel and look.

I don’t know how to sit still and wait for the final release. I’m ready to buy two PS5 copies for family co-op, recommend it to everyone, and gift it to every friend.

A gorgeous game with an interesting story and a well-developed world that is absolutely ruined by being hilariously overtuned and needlessly difficult. 

I'll revisit No Rest For The Wicked again closer to 1.0 when the devs realize how stupidly hard this game is and inevitably fix it. Keep in mind, this is coming from a Souls LOVER who's played these kinds of games from PS3, 360, PS4, XB1 and PS5, all the way up to PC, multiple times over including Sekiro, Bloodborne, all the knock-offs like Code Vein, community mods and everything else. I don't mind a challenge when the challenge feels fair and makes sense, but this game is hard for all the WRONG reasons. And before anyone asks:

• Super spongy trash mobs still 80% you in one hit, so every encounter feels artificially drawn out and tedious
• Durability loss on death punishes learning enemy move sets (why are we bringing back archaic, failed systems like this?)
• Finite meals/potions punishes learning enemy move sets (why are we departing from refillable estus, a system that has worked well for years?)
• Way too grindy to replace mats to make more food and repair gear after repeated deaths while learning enemy move sets
• Absolutely unforgiving parry windows, and I mean brutal, plus the parry itself still sucks even when you land it (because spongy enemies)
• Back stabs are nearly impossible to land and most enemies flat out can't be back stabbed and it's also garbage (because spongy enemies)
• Shields aren't 100% block so far, so you're constantly taking damage unless you roll dodge everything (which leaves you with 0 stamina to parry or attack)
• Enemies stun lock you very easily
• Fighting 2 or more enemies is basically a GG, nearly impossible to win and the aggro range extends past what's visible on screen, so mobs just come running from off-screen constantly to catch you off guard
• Sneaking is laughably terrible
• You are essentially 'heavy' at all times unless you wear trash armor (I sacrificed other stats to dump 10 points into weight, which is a lot btw, and I still barely fit into the 'normal' range with starter gear, so now my stats are trash and I've gained nothing for it)
• Stamina is severely lacking, you're always out of it, even if you understand Souls-like stamina management
• Can't easily swap between the 15+ unique meals or potions in your inventory in the heat of combat, plus heals have a LONG cool down for some reason
• 'Bonfires' don't restore health or healing items
• Inventory is always full and getting it all back to your 'stash' or a vendor is very tedious (plus the stash is way too small)
• The amount of backtracking you have to do in this game is absurd so far, which is exacerbated by the hideous and borderline useless map they give us
• Fall damage is comically strong
• Control scheme gets you killed constantly (you have to tap A to dodge, but you also have to hold it to climb, but holding it also makes you dash, which leads to you accidentally running or rolling off of tight edges way too often, which means you die to the comically strong fall damage, which means your gear takes damage, which means you have to repair it, which means you have to farm again... you see where this is going.)

The list goes on and on and on and I haven't even touched on the terrible performance or optimization that everyone else has mentioned. Those are absolutely valid criticisms. You can't have a game suffering from volatile frame rate changes with an air tight combat system like this. It gets you killed. Constantly. And again, before anyone asks, I have great hardware. Liquid cooled 13th gen i9, 64GB of RAM, M.2 drive and a 3080 ti GPU.

Review:

Okay, let me preface this by saying that I did enjoy this game for the first twenty or so hours. It's not a bad game, and I wish I could give a mixed review instead of a negative one. However, as an older gamer who grew up on more straightforward games, I really think "No Rest for the Wicked" suffers from many of the problems that plague a lot of modern games. Mainly, the following:

-There's an incredibly time-wasting resource collection grind that isn't fun or interesting. Instead, it resorts to a quicktime event type system where you need to time the swings of your tools perfectly to get the best results. Perhaps that's fun for others (and if it is for you, then I recommend this game), but I personally grew increasingly bored and frustrated by it.

-There's a tacked-on rogue-lite dungeon that feels wildly out of place in what I thought was a souls-like game.

-There's FOMO daily and weekly quests that are more akin to a live service multiplayer game (or MMORPG) than a single player one.

-There's the obligatory crafting system that really doesn't add much to the game besides more bloat. I was so inundated with crap by the time I gave up that I really never even touched the crafting beyond slotting runes or gems.

-There's an odd diablo-style "loot, loot, as far as the eye can see" system where your bags fill up so fast that you are forced to return to town frequently just to sell/disenchant the loot. Less would have been more rewarding in this situation. Instead, I ended up sighing whenever more weapons dropped or were found.

-The level design (as mentioned in the positives below), is great in how it utilizes space, but it's also maze-like, meaning you waste even more time running around looking for the one hidden jump you're supposed to find to progress.

-Why is stamina so costly for the most basic of activities, even after you've buffed your stamina amount? You can attack maybe 3-4 times before running out. Even Dark Souls had better stamina than that.

A few positives:

-This might be the most gorgeous game I've seen in a long time.
-The voice acting is excellent and the story is passable.
-The level design is actually very impressive in how it utilizes vertical spaces and secret areas, not to mention kicking down ladders or opening up doors that create shortcuts between older paths and newer ones. 
-The combat is pretty fun and varied.
-The weapons are all different.

Basically, the gist of what I'm saying is this: this game has no idea what it wants to be. Parts of it are souls-like, others are like a MMORPG or live service game, others are rogue-lite, others are like a mobile game or DDR, and even more are like a looter shooter / Diablo-style action game. Oh, and add a crafting system too. Why so much bloat? The game could be streamlined and become just fine if it took out much of that nonsense. 

This is the inherent problem with so many games nowadays: they're trying to be a lifestyle rather than a game. There's nothing wrong with a 10-hour or 20-hour solo experience. Why stretch that to 50-100 hours? 

I wanted to like this game, but I just grew tired of the bloat. I can play three sessions of a more efficient game in the duration it takes me to do the simplest progression in this one. And it's frustrating, because I really believe there is a great game underneath all the fat here. I wish the designers had just trimmed away all the BS and gotten to the core experience. Some of us have limited gaming time and thus don't want to waste hours upon hours chopping trees in what was advertised to be an action RPG.

So, if you like jack-of-all-trades games, then you'll probably love this one. I don't, so I didn't.

This is an extremely difficult game to review.  
  
On one hand, it's a fantastically detailed, Dark-Souls esque-game with a fascinating progression system.  
  
On the other hand, it's a combination of mobile multi-hour wait times (In a single player game), an NPC that only spawns on specific times over the weekend of the real world time, and "I Wanna Be The Guy" style difficulty with checkpoints a mile apart that kill you in impossible ways. Stun-locked to death by an off-screen enemy? A "jump to your death" style platform that's impossible to determine? Camera angles that make "Fall to your death" holes impossible to see? Combine this and many more with a "Let's send you back multiple minutes on every death!" system, and it shifts from "Challenging" to "Difficult for the sake of being difficult" bordering on tedium.

It reminds me of the difficulty system of a P2W mobile game - The difficulty is tedium and annoyance more than challenge. Need a specific resource? Either spend an hour running around an area you've cleared 20 times over, or quit and come back when it's respawned the following real-time day. Boss you're going to challenge a hundred times over to perfect the dodge mechanics to actually kill it? How about a 30 second run to it each time! Put the wrong stat into your build 10 hours in so you can't use a better weapon? Tough luck - You're stuck with your broken build - Go grind some more! 

As it stand - Wait a few months. It's Early Access-ness shows, but there is something there that could be awesome - It's just not there yet, and you'll cut yourself along the way looking for it.

Okay, so where do I start...?

First of all, there's so much great potential in this game. But I've never felt so conflicted about a title, and sadly can not recommend it (yet) in it's current state.

I'm posting this review (and I usually never take the time to write reviews) in the hopes it reaches moon / Thomas, because I want to love this game and for it to be better. The world - as usual with moon studio titles - is just plain beautiful. I love discovering secret paths or chests, hidden by the forced perspective. The music is pure bliss too. The combat scratches an itch I barely feel in other games, except the FROM SOFTWARE titles. It's meaty, calculated, and the weapons have cool distinct movesets. 

But my god, do I have many pet peeves with this title. And since praising the good stuff won't improve the game, I'll focus on the areas that need improvements / changes in my opinion. I'm not dunking on the game, I want to give constructive criticism and suggestions. I know I don't have many hours of playtime yet, but please Thomas, if you read this, feel free to add me / hit me up. I'm always up for hearing thoughts, discussing stuff, and I watched quite a few of the dev streams on twitch recently. I think the game wants to be and do too much at the same time and is in danger of feature creep and is a slog in many aspects already. Let's go:

1. The combat - while great in 1v1 encounters - turns very chaotic and many times frustrating when you're facing off more than one enemy. It doesn't really feel designed around that. The biggest problem here is the stamina system and the base movement speed. It's just too slow. You not only have to dodge, but basically sprint all the time as the character (even with medium equipment load) is moving at the pace of a turtle. You find yourself constantly out of stamina, even when doing the old dodge/get two hits in/dodge away combo.

2. While we're at the stamina issue: It feels out of place for swimming and climbing. We could argue about climbing, since the sections are usually visible and you can judge if you'd be able to make it. But for swimming it just straight feels off. With the forced perspective of the camera (which I love) and the nature of bodies of water being much bigger than a vines climbing section, many times you won't know when the next patch of solid ground comes up. Swimming into the unknown, just to instantly die in front of the next beach when out of stamina has to be the most frustrating feeling ever. If you're scared players would cheese encounters by kiting / swimming around and enemy, get a hit and then retreat to the water, just enable stamina for swimming while in combat only. Or make the player slowly lose health, instead of instant death. But in my humble opinion: Outside of combat swimming and climbing shouldn't trigger the stamina bar.

3. PLEASE get rid of the weapon- and especially tools- degradation. This system never added any meaningful mechanics to any title. It's just another annoying thing you have to do when dying a few times. Go back to town, pass a negligible gold check, teleport back to the area. You already have enough penalties from dying. Being teleported back to the last checkpoint, not regaining the consumables you used in the fights. This on top just feels tedious and does not add any meaningful depth or choices for the player. 

4. I know this has been brought up many times already and you guys already work on changes for that system, but I would still like to reiterate that the current system of stats and their requirements to wield weapons feels super restrictive and actively hinders experimenting. It works in the souls games because weapons mostly don't drop randomly. You know where to find what and when, and can plan your build around it. But for a random loot system it feels bad not being able to equip a dropped weapon, because I specced in the 'wrong' stats. Please be more like Diablo / Path of Exile, and less like FROM games in this regard.

5. Let's talk housing / base building / resource gathering: I like the fundamental idea of repairing buildings and shortcuts in the city. But the building projects having timers feels out of place. This stuff belongs in mobile games like Clash of Clans (which I play). Once I gathered the necessary resources (which already takes too long for many) it should just complete right when I pay for the project. It doesn't add anything to the game and making me wait for it to complete feels like a slog. If I wanted to play harvest moon or stardew valley.... I'd play just that. But this is mainly an ARPG (or should be). Gathering the resources also feels more like work than fun. The perfect gathering system is a small improvement in theory, but after I realised how little is to be gained from that, I stopped bothering with it. You need to hit perfects the whole way through, just to get one additional piece of wood. Great... Sure it becomes a bit faster this way, but it doesn't feel rewarding. Gathering overall takes too long (with and without perfects) and breaks the flow of the game too much. Since resources are so scarce, you feel the need to stop at every source and hack / dig away. I want to move through the world, fight enemies, discover stuff. Not spend 50% of my area traversal time stopping in front of trees. And let me re-iterate again: The weapons- and tools- degradation makes this even more un-fun. Make it overall faster to gather, give us more resources. make perfects worth it.

6. While I have a pretty high-end rig and overall performance is solid, there seems to be a fundamental problem with the way assets are being streamed in. The game runs at a solid 120 fps, but whenever I trigger a loading zone for the next chucks of geometry and textures, i get a massive and very noticeable drop in frames.

7. The single press / long press menu bar. Just open the complete menu UI on single press and get rid of this functionality. This current in-between "menu bar, but not really" on single press feels so useless.

8. While not a problem yet, it might become one in the future with the current tendency of feature creep: I saw Thomas experiment with a 3rd person camera and some people were really fond of it. I know many gamers want all games to be everything. But I think following this path and potentially making this an option would be of detriment to the game and it's identity. I like the fixed perspective and the game and world is clearly designed around it. The way paths and chests are hidden by perspective. 3rd person would just kill this aspect. Please don't waste resources on developing such an option. Have a vision of what your game should be. And it can't and shouldn't be everything.

This game is really pretty, visually appealing, highly stylized and looks very polished, sounds polished as well. The world looks great. This art style lends itself to the game and its story really well and it shows. 

My gripes with this game is that while emulating the souls-like combat formula, I think it sorely misses the mark, at least for me. Now, I've only played DS3 which isn't much, but one thing that always pops up in my mind when think of this combat system is - rhythm. The combat has rhythm from the very beginning and keeps that rhythm until the end. 

No Rest For the Wicked, to me at least, doesn't have that crucial rhythm that makes souls-like games tick. While Dark Souls employs 3rd person cam, No rest for the wicked is asymmetrical. With that it comes with a myriad of issues; really hard time tracking your stamina as you're rolling around, or just attacking, getting attacked or keeping eyes on your poise meter. I am not sure why they decided to center this particular element of the HUD in the center in a small circle around your character, and not in a static place on the screen as you would in any other game in the genre. 

Exploration in this game while initially fun and interesting, becomes quite bothersome after you've gone around the same area 10+ times. For some reason, someone made the choice to turn the exploration into an active part of material gathering and grinding in this game. It's especially clear after you reach the town and the entire first area 'resets' with new mobs, and, you guessed it, every single chest in that area has been reset as well. 

This becomes incredibly annoying since you're not going to find anything different, and the sense of wonder, and discovery is quickly lost as you understand that the game wants you to keep opening the same chests over and over to get materials that you can use to upgrade, or use them for something else. 

Which leads me to my next pain point - the pacing and overall progression of this game is all over the place. The game just inundates you with loot at the beginning. Not good loot, just loot, akin to Destiny 2. Oh, and you have limited inventory slots. And if you happen to explore around the first area a lot, you would need to delete items to make space :). Nifty. 

You can't salvage any of the equipment for materials mind you, you can just sell them, which allows you to gather quite a lot of money early on if you explore, and re-explore every nook and cranny. Which makes it completely wack cuz you get a shit ton of money early on, but you can't really upgrade your gear all that much cuz every item past +1 and +2 requires a lot more materials that you need to refine, and some that you don't have access to yet.  

Refining materials can only happen if you upgrade each individual shop in the town. But upgrading the structures has a literal time gate on it. So if you just want to upgrade your blacksmith, refine some shit, upgrade and get on with exploring/ fighting -  tough luck, idiot, you have to wait an hour.  

Pair this time gate with areas that don't refresh upon your death, and enemies that spawn after a timer, unsure how long, and you end up just walking around aimlessly in areas hoping to find something new, more loot, or materials. 

Material gathering while engaging gets annoying really fast. Having to repeatedly spam the button at the right time to maybe get extra, or rarer materials feels gratifying at first, but when you end up running around empty areas cuz you got nothing to do, and you just decide to chop a tree it feels quite bad tbh. 

At the end I feel that while these systems are hand picked from various games, the implementation, at least at this stage, is not very good.

This game suffers from probably the biggest lack of QOL features I've played in 30+ years in gaming. While I love the art style, the story, and to a degree - the combat, the rest feels half-baked, obtuse, and unnecessarily punitive to the point I found myself going 'Why??' multiple times in my playthrough. Here's just a short list.

- You can only fast travel back to the last fast travel point. Hope you enjoy running through the same zones, repeatedly, over and over. Oh, and everything respawns in said zones constantly.
- There are no descriptions on anything, anywhere. There's something like over a hundred enchantments, none of them are explained anywhere. No tool tips, no explanation, no description, literally nothing.
- Likewise, there are several dozen if not more runes (special abilities) in the game. These are never explained anywhere. Not what they do, how much they cost, damage output. Nothing. Just 'Dash Break'. Oh...ok?
- Continuing in the mystery meat category, you cannot get a preview of any weapon in the game. You will be forced to blindly allocate stats starting at the beginning of the game which may or may not absolutely butcher your character. Some weapons require high allocation in one stat, some require a mix. Want to try out Great Swords? Just kidding you cant because you decided to go Dexterity. You have NO IDEA what weapons are even out there until you find them, but by then its too late. Supposedly theres a scythe in the game, would love to try it, no idea what stats it needs and I probably cant. "Just respec" you say?.....
- You can't respec until you play the Crucible and farm it out. You can't farm it out until about level 15, which is over 25 hours into the game give or take and it requires currency to spend. So enjoy that grind every time you just want to TRY a weapon that you might even hate. Youll have to refarm everything just to respec back.
- Ive yet to figure out the purpose of crafting armor. Ive been playing for 25 hours, I have enough resources to make one full set of the Tallbearers armor. With how enchanting works, there's about a 30% chance the gear gets cursed and becomes essentially worthless. What's the point?
- Need to remove a rune? Destroys your weapon. Need to remove that gem? Sorry, not a thing. Want to simply move runes around to assign them to different hotkeys? Nope. 
- Heavy armor gets high armor class (physical), but the worst resist values against Fire, Shock, etc. Conversely, light armor gets low AC and high resist. ....Why? So basically the game prevents you from just being slow and tanky because if you do, youll be strong to ONE THING ONLY (physical) with the worst resistances. So why wear heavy armor? Again, contrary to every use of 'heavy armor' in every game literally ever.....   
- The camera angle is never where it needs to be and cant be controlled. You will routinely have to navigate narrow corners and tight spaces where you can't even see where you're going, particularly when descending. The gameworld will constantly obscure your screen, as well. Buildings, roofs, tree canopies - there's about a 50/50 shot that the game catches it and sets it transparent, or not and you're just screwed. Additionally, the camera is constantly floating around, pulling out, moving in, trying to show a panoramic, etc. Like, just leave the damn camera alone, you aren't Martin Scorsese. 
- Why are bows an offhand item...? I burned a plague ichor to unlock a 2nd main hand to have a bow as an alternate weapon. Instead, I go to equip it and it puts itself in the offhand slot....the off hand slot which I am using DUAL GAUNTLETS in the main hand. Explain this to me please? Worth noting nowhere on any weapon does it say 'Mainhand' or 'Offhand'. This is what I'm talking about, how did this get past QA?? This is basic stuff, I am just floored at how lacking it is.
- A litany of bugs to contend with as well. Ive opened chests or cooked food and suddenly immolated into death. Ive been stuck in run mode with both hands off the M&K. Ive been stuck in the map. Ive failed to grab ladders and fallen to my death countless times. Ive lost game audio. Etc, etc, etc...
- And now the last and potentially worst bit, the movement. You will die constantly and not to enemies, but to fall damage. Your character will religiously throw herself off every cliff, bridge, ledge, and outcrop possible. The movement controls in this game are the absolute worst. DO NOT even attempt to play this on M&K. "Run" is Shift, right? But unlike every other game ever made since the dawn of time, holding shift doesnt 'enable' you to run using WASD...it actually makes your character run in the direction of your mouse cursor. So  you are simultaneously moving your character with WASD while also potentially trying to go a different direction while holding shift depending on where your mouse cursor is. Oh, and did I mention that attack animations are queued? Click 3 times, you will attack 3 times, even if you no longer want nor need to. Now, couple this with the fact your character doesnt just attack, they ALWAYS step towards the target and attack and you're constantly rolling/attacking into places you have no business or desire being but the system and mechanics screw you over and work against you in every way imaginable. 

I could go on and on with the frustrating and mind boggling decisions being made here. This is basic stuff, standard QOL that seemingly every game has yet at every turn this game actively gets in your way, confusing you and obfuscating every key decision and integral game mechanic. Its a lesson in perseverance and frustration, neither of which the standard gamer is going to have time for. If you enjoy driving blindfolded, I encourage you to give this a try. Just don't be surprised when you slam into a wall going 80. 

NOTE: I will amend this review after EA if these issues are addressed.

I bought this game when it was first released originally in April 2024 then immediately refunded it due to the game being almost unplayable on Steam deck which will color most of my review so far. I decided to pick it up again nearly a year later when it went on sale and read online about the game;s current state now that it is playable on the deck. From what i played so far, was pretty fun but unstable. i'm still in the opening area after the first boss, trying my hand on a side quest. This game crashes. a. lot. i understand what i was getting myself into, when i bought it at early access. it didn't stop me from playing a whole good chunk of morning to noon. it works fine if the graphical setting was set at either balanced or performance, the game has enough of a beautiful aesthetic to mask whatever graphical short comings my experience during play time. speaking of which: the Art direction is Gorgeous. i love the painterly way the characters are depicted, not too anatomically accurate but enough to give it a stylized feel to it. absolutely lovely aesthetic. some nitpick to add and hopefully be addressed by the developers, is the difficulty to use consumable items. i thought it was my d-pad at first on the deck and decided to switch to the big screen with a game pad but pressing up or down takes up so much time especially when you're under the hilt of an enemy sword. i understand that there are cool downs in using consumables or specifically health items you have to draw your focus away from the action toward what usually is a single press with other ARPGs. another issue i have is maybe moving the stamina bar away from the character and put it near where the other UI bars are. it's hard to tell sometimes if you're close to running out of stamina without squinting hard enough, and lastly, the stamina regeneration is way too slow to recover. i get that i can put points on endurance but that only elongates the bar and not increase the generation speed. absolutely deadly in the beginning if you decided to the speed-dex build. in conclusion: will I recommend this game to anyone interested? absolutely but keep in mind all the caveats i have given. there are diamond and platinum beneath all the hard crashes and frame rate issues but this car is too fun of a ride to give up on so soon now that i can drive it. just mind the chitty-chitty bang-bangs.
